routing_reason: Existing Stripe Billing source update: full new raw + matched prior raw + current source; preserve version, UI variant, client/server, state and dated evidence boundaries; no semantic assumptions from collection diff alone.
findings: The November same-URL capture is a 14-line variant index with purpose text and two navigation links, not a full SEPA subscription guide (new 5-14). It identifies a full hosted web variant and an advanced web/elements variant, but contains no API schema, payment states, mandate instructions, webhook outcomes, IBAN tests or account eligibility. The 1763-line diff is almost entirely removal of old variant content from this unparameterized rendering and does not prove feature removal.

The May same-URL raw contained both full hosted Checkout and advanced integration variants (old 8-10, 1027-1033). Its hosted example creates a subscription Checkout Session with sepa_debit and at least one recurring price (old 188-214), and its delayed-notification section distinguishes authorization at checkout.session.completed from later async success or invoice.paid (old 236-269). Preserve these as May snapshot evidence, not claims established by new index.

The May advanced variant includes customer-configured Accounts v2 and Customers v1 branches, with version qualification for Accounts v2 (old 1053-1097), and distinguishes latest invoice confirmation_secret from pending_setup_intent where no payment is collected up front (old 1101-1145). It documents mandate collection/client confirmation and default payment methods (old 1148-1407). The November index does not settle whether those instructions changed in the linked variants.

The current source and concept need bounded historical-summary corrections despite the November index being navigation-only. Source 13, 61 and concept 116 say 20+ IBAN countries and source 61 lists SK and SI, but the May raw has 19 country headings per variant, with no SK or SI tables (old 399-644, 1417-1662). Source 13 calls Checkout recommended without support in the matched May guide. The May advanced variant both recommends a separate Payment Element build guide for new users and mounts a Payment Element in its own sample (old 1033, 1169-1205, 1242-1257); its confirmation calls are confirmSepaDebitPayment or confirmSepaDebitSetup, not source 30's confirmPayment (old 1259-1262, 1283-1296).

Source 41 narrows invoice.paid to renewal success, but the May event table says payment succeeded without that limitation, and its webhook example explicitly permits invoice.paid before checkout.session.completed, fulfills the purchase, and records a paid period (old 257-261, 303-330). Preserve the authorization-versus-paid distinction without restricting invoice.paid to renewals.

The old guide's sample product amounts/currencies and test IBANs are examples, not SEPA availability guarantees; notably one API price code uses currency usd while surrounding examples say EUR (old 103-166). New index says nothing about customer, merchant, account, bank, payment or settlement eligibility.
substantive_changes: No substantive payment, mandate, API, webhook or eligibility change is established by the November unparameterized index; the observable change is rendering/navigation to two query-parameter variants (new 9-14 versus old 8-10, 1027-1033).

The new capture supports routing by full hosted and advanced integration labels only. It does not supply evidence to replace the May source's factual SEPA flow, delay warning, test tables, or Accounts v2 qualification. A source_required_update disposition is nevertheless warranted to correct already present misleading May summaries in source 13, 30, 41, 61 and reciprocal concept 105, 116, without attributing those corrections to November behavior.
